thread:
jordan: Heads up — customer 'coinbase-lite' reports a sudden spike in latency and 403s. They were pinned to eu-west-1 but traces show requests hitting us-east. Can someone look?

support-bot: Thanks @jordan — creating escalation ticket #INC-8952 and pinging infra. ETA 10m :rotating_light:

maya: Customer id and example request id?

jordan: customer_id=cb-lite-984; sample request id=req_0x9a8bcd; reported when model inference started at ~11:22 UTC.

ryan-eng: Looking at routing logs for cb-lite-984... I see affinity_pin_expired events around 11:20, followed by fallback to hosted pool in us-east-1. Sticky TTL was 24h but last refresh failed. Repro info below.

ryan-eng: snippet from routing log:
```
2026-03-17T11:20:31Z INFO route_decision tenant=cb-lite-984 prev_pin=eu-west-1 pin_refresh_error=403 token_scope_mismatch fallback=hosted-us-east-1
2026-03-17T11:20:31Z DEBUG affinity_pin_expired tenant=cb-lite-984 ttl_remaining=0
```

maya: Token scope mismatch? Why would pin refresh 403? That usually means the pin-refresh request used an opaque token tied to region.

ryan-eng: Exactly. The refresh uses the customer's key pool that was created in eu-west-1. When the refresh hit the hosted control-plane in us-east (during an outage window), the control-plane rejected it due to region-scoped signing keys -> 403.

ryan-eng: Quick repro (from our internal runbook):
```
# simulate expired pin + control-plane region mismatch
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer opaque-token-eu" -H "X-Serving-Region: eu-west-1" https://control-plane.us-east-1.redwood.internal/v1/pins/refresh -v
# response
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"token_scope_mismatch","msg":"refresh token not valid in this control-plane region"}
```

infra-sre-bot: Observed host-level backpressure on eu-west GPU pool at 11:18-11:24. Autoscaler temporarily drained some nodes which increased refresh latency and coincided with control-plane failover.

billing-bot: Noting spike: hosted pool usage + customer billed usage increased ~12x during 11:20-11:30 window. Ticketed to billing for potential credit: BLG-412.

elaine: Short-term mitigation: force re-pin the customer to eu-west-1 via admin API and increase pin TTL while we patch key validation. Command:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer admin-token" https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/tenants/cb-lite-984/pins -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","ttl":2592000}'
```

maya: Also need to add a fallback policy change: prefer same-region hosted pool (if available) before global hosted to prevent cross-region auth mismatches.

ryan-eng: Action items: 1) Re-pin customer (in progress) 2) Patch control-plane to accept cross-region token-refresh proxies (PR #3487) 3) Change fallback policy to prefer local-region hosted pool (RFC drafted) 4) Billing review BLG-412.

jordan: Thanks team. I updated INC-8952 with notes and assigned to @ryan-eng and @elaine. Will follow up with customer about temporary credit and ETA for permanent fix.

support-bot: INC-8952 updated. Closing this thread and moving details to incident doc: https://redwood.hit/INC-8952 :white_check_mark:
